title: Web Server on Pico W
description: Learn to create a web server on Raspberry Pi Pico W to remotely control devices through a browser.
objectives: Configure Pico W as a web server
Send HTTP commands to control hardware

warnings: Always use resistor with LEDs to avoid burning them

theory.webserver: A web server is a program that responds to HTTP requests. The Pico W can act as a server, allowing you to control hardware through a web browser.
theory.http: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the protocol used for web communication. Main methods: GET (retrieve data) and POST (send data).
theory.restapi: REST API uses URLs to represent resources. Example: GET /led/status returns LED state, POST /led/on turns LED on.

steps.title: Connect Pico W to WiFi
details: Add 'Print' block to show received IP

steps.title: Create Web Server
steps.description: Configure HTTP server on Pico W

steps.title: Create HTML Interface
steps.description: Develop a web page to control LED
details: Create HTML page with 'On' and 'Off' buttons
Add CSS to style the interface
Implement JavaScript to make AJAX requests

steps.title: Implement LED Control
details: In /led/on route, set GPIO 15 to HIGH
In /led/off route, set GPIO 15 to LOW

bipesProject.description: Pre-configured BIPES project with web server and LED control. Open, configure your WiFi and deploy to Pico W.

troubleshooting.problem: Pico W doesn't connect to WiFi
solutions: Check if SSID and password are correct
Make sure network is 2.4GHz (Pico W doesn't support 5GHz)
Move Pico W closer to router
Restart Pico W and try again
Check IP assigned to Pico W in serial terminal
Make sure you're on the same WiFi network
Test LED manually with 'Digital Write' block
Check if resistor is correctly positioned
